evidence: Nestled within the bustling heart of Hanoi’s Đống Đa District, at 58 Văn Miếu Street, lies the Temple of Literature - Quốc Tử Giám complex, a revered site that has stood as a testament to Vietnam’s rich educational heritage since its founding in 1070 under Emperor Lý Thánh Tông of the Lý dynasty. The complex, a UNESCO World Heritage site and a national special relic, encompasses a myriad of historically significant areas, among which the Nhap Dao section stands out as the introductory courtyard, marking the threshold between the secular world and the sacred realm of learning and spiritual growth.
